name: airtable-mcp
label: Airtable (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/airtable-mcp/mcp. Airtable's own remote MCP server for reading and writing bases, reached with a personal access token; the token's own scopes and base access decide what it can see, and nothing here widens them.

name: apify-mcp
label: Apify (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/apify-mcp/. Apify's own remote MCP server for running its scraping actors, reached with an Apify API token; Apify's SSE transport was removed in April 2026, so this is the streamable-HTTP address and the only one.

name: atlassian-mcp
label: Atlassian Rovo (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/atlassian-mcp/v2/mcp. Atlassian's own remote MCP server for Jira and Confluence, reached with a service-account API key. An organisation admin has to turn API-token authentication on first, and the other documented token shape — a personal API token as basic auth over your own email address — is not offered here because the username is yours and we will not guess it.

name: cloudflare-mcp
label: Cloudflare API (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/cloudflare-mcp/mcp. Cloudflare's own remote MCP server for its API, reached with a Cloudflare API token. Cloudflare runs a further fifteen product servers on their own hostnames — docs, radar, observability and the rest — and each is a separate address, so this entry reaches the API one alone.

name: datadog-eu-mcp
label: Datadog EU1 (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/datadog-eu-mcp/v1/mcp. The same Datadog MCP server for the EU1 site, reached with a personal or service account token; a token belongs to one site, and the US, AP and UK sites are further hosts again.

name: datadog-mcp
label: Datadog US1 (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/datadog-mcp/v1/mcp. Datadog's own remote MCP server for the US1 site, reached with a personal or service account token. Datadog can restrict this server to an IP allowlist, in which case our egress address has to be on it; each Datadog site is a different host, and the government sites are not served at all.

name: github-mcp
label: GitHub (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/github-mcp/mcp. GitHub's own remote MCP server — repository, issue, pull request and search tools — reached with a personal access token. GitHub also offers one-click OAuth for this endpoint and that path is not ours to perform, so store a token; a token whose shape GitHub does not recognise is rejected before it is ever checked, with a 400 rather than a 401.

name: huggingface-mcp
label: Hugging Face (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/huggingface-mcp/mcp. Hugging Face's own remote MCP server for searching models, datasets and Spaces and calling Space tools, reached with a Hugging Face token; it is stateless, so nothing here holds a session on your behalf.

name: intercom-eu-mcp
label: Intercom EU (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/intercom-eu-mcp/mcp. The same Intercom MCP server for an EU-hosted workspace, reached with an Intercom access token. A token belongs to one region, so a US workspace needs intercom-mcp instead; Intercom does not yet serve Australian workspaces at all.

name: intercom-mcp
label: Intercom US (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/intercom-mcp/mcp. Intercom's own remote MCP server for a US-hosted workspace, reached with an Intercom access token. An EU workspace is a different address — intercom-eu-mcp — and an Australian one is not served at all; the handshake and the tool listing answer any token, so a wrong one is only refused when a tool is actually called.

name: linear-mcp
label: Linear (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/linear-mcp/mcp. Linear's own remote MCP server — issues, projects and cycles — reached with a Linear API key in the Authorization header, which Linear documents as an alternative to its OAuth flow. Note the header differs from Linear's GraphQL API, where the same key is sent bare with no Bearer word.

name: monday-mcp
label: monday.com (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/monday-mcp/mcp. monday.com's own remote MCP server for boards, items and updates, reached with a personal API token, which monday documents as the path for clients that cannot do its OAuth flow. Its SSE address is deprecated and is not what this reaches.

name: neon-mcp
label: Neon (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/neon-mcp/mcp. Neon's own remote MCP server for managing Postgres projects, branches and queries, reached with a Neon API key. Neon's deprecated SSE endpoint is a separate address and does not accept an API key at all, so this is the only shape a stored key can reach.

name: perplexity-mcp
label: Perplexity (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/perplexity-mcp/mcp. Perplexity's own remote MCP server for its search and research tools, reached with a Perplexity API key. This is a search surface rather than a model one: a chat completion goes to Perplexity's ordinary API, which is a different upstream.

name: posthog-mcp
label: PostHog (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/posthog-mcp/mcp. PostHog's own remote MCP server for queries, insights, feature flags and errors, reached with a personal API key. PostHog's EU customers are told to use a different host whose full address it does not publish, so this entry is the US one.

name: postman-eu-mcp
label: Postman EU (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/postman-eu-mcp/mcp. The same Postman MCP server for the EU region, reached with a Postman API key; Postman documents the EU host as accepting an API key and nothing else, so this is the whole of its authentication.

name: postman-mcp
label: Postman US (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/postman-mcp/mcp. Postman's own remote MCP server for collections, environments and specs, reached with a Postman API key. Postman serves three narrower tool sets at /minimal, /code and /learn on the same host, and the EU region is a separate address.

name: sanity-mcp
label: Sanity (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/sanity-mcp/. Sanity's own remote MCP server for content in a Sanity project, reached with a Sanity API token, which Sanity documents as the way to skip its OAuth flow entirely.

name: shortio-mcp
label: Short.io (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/shortio-mcp/mcp. Short.io's own remote MCP server for short links and their statistics, reached with a secret key sent as the whole Authorization value with no Bearer word, which is what we send.

name: supabase-mcp
label: Supabase (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/supabase-mcp/mcp. Supabase's own remote MCP server, reached with a Supabase personal access token. It covers every organisation that token can see unless the client narrows it with a project_ref query parameter, which is the client's to add and not something stored here.

name: telnyx-mcp
label: Telnyx (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/telnyx-mcp/v2/mcp. Telnyx's own remote MCP server over its v2 API, reached with a Telnyx API key; Telnyx's own server card says this version does not do OAuth at all, so a key is the only way in, and its older SSE address is a different path.

name: zapier-mcp
label: Zapier (MCP)
note: Point an MCP client at /gw/zapier-mcp/api/v1/connect. Zapier's own remote MCP server, reached with a connection token generated at mcp.zapier.com. The token names the server and the actions you chose there, so what this reaches is whatever that configuration exposes and nothing wider; Zapier also accepts the token as a query parameter, and its own documentation prefers the header for the reason a URL ends up in logs.
